content: Chloramphenicol has the potential to increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of various drugs by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction can lead to heightened drug toxicity or adverse effects. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations for each drug: 1. Guanfacine: Chloramphenicol increases guanfacine levels. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. Monitor for adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 2. Haloperidol: Chloramphenicol increases haloperidol levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Ibrutinib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases ibrutinib levels. This combination is contraindicated. 4. Infigratinib: Chloramphenicol increases infigratinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Irinotecan: Chloramphenicol increases irinotecan levels. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Irinotecan Liposomal: Chloramphenicol increases irinotecan liposomal levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Ivosidenib: Chloramphenicol increases ivosidenib levels. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Ixabepilone: Chloramphenicol increases ixabepilone levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Lapatinib: Chloramphenicol increases lapatinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Larotrectinib: Chloramphenicol increases larotrectinib levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce larotrectinib dose by 50% if unavoidable. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3–5 half-lives. 11. Lefamulin: Chloramphenicol increases lefamulin levels. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 12. Lemborexant: Chloramphenicol increases lemborexant levels. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 13. Leniolisib: Chloramphenicol increases leniolisib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Levomilnacipran: Chloramphenicol increases levomilnacipran levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Lorlatinib: Chloramphenicol increases lorlatinib levels. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives. 16. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Chloramphenicol increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Lurbinectedin: Chloramphenicol increases lurbinectedin levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dose by 50% if unavoidable. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 18. Mefloquine: Chloramphenicol increases mefloquine levels, potentially increasing toxicity. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 19. Microbiota Oral: Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of microbiota oral therapy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 20. Midostaurin: Chloramphenicol increases midostaurin levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Mifepristone: Chloramphenicol increases mifepristone levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Nilotinib: Chloramphenicol increases nilotinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Nirogacestat: Chloramphenicol increases nirogacestat levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Nisoldipine: Chloramphenicol increases nisoldipine levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Olaparib: Chloramphenicol increases olaparib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Chloramphenicol increases the levels of this combination. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Palbociclib: Chloramphenicol increases palbociclib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Palovarotene: Chloramphenicol increases palovarotene levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Pazopanib: Chloramphenicol increases pazopanib levels. This combination is contraindicated. 30. Pexidartinib: Chloramphenicol increases pexidartinib levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dose if unavoidable. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 half-lives. 31. Pimavanserin: Chloramphenicol increases pimavanserin levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Pimozide: Chloramphenicol increases pimozide levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Pirtobrutinib: Chloramphenicol increases pirtobrutinib levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dose by 50 mg if unavoidable. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 34. Ponatinib: Chloramphenicol increases ponatinib levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dose to the next lower level. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 half-lives. 35. Pralsetinib: Chloramphenicol increases pralsetinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Quetiapine: Chloramphenicol increases quetiapine levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Ranolazine: Chloramphenicol increases ranolazine levels. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Red Yeast Rice: Chloramphenicol increases the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis due to elevated creatine kinase levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Regorafenib: Chloramphenicol increases regorafenib levels. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Repotrectinib: Chloramphenicol increases repotrectinib levels. Avoid coadministration or discontinue the inhibitor for 3–5 half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 41. Ribociclib: Chloramphenicol increases ribociclib levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce the starting dose to 400 mg/day if unavoidable. 42. Rimegepant: Chloramphenicol increases rimegepant levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Ritonavir: Chloramphenicol increases ritonavir levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Ruxolitinib: Chloramphenicol increases ruxolitinib levels. Reduce the dosage in patients with myelofibrosis or polycythemia vera. No dose adjustment is necessary for graft-versus-host disease. 45. Saxagliptin: Chloramphenicol increases saxagliptin levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Selumetinib: Chloramphenicol increases selumetinib levels. Avoid coadministration or reduce the dosage if unavoidable. Resume the prior dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 half-lives. 47. Sildenafil: Chloramphenicol increases sildenafil levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 48. Siponimod: Chloramphenicol increases siponimod levels. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with CYP2C9 inhibitors. 49. Sirolimus: Chloramphenicol increases sirolimus levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 50. Sonidegib: Chloramphenicol increases sonidegib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Sparsentan: Chloramphenicol increases sparsentan levels. Avoid coadministration or interrupt treatment if unavoidable. Resume with dose titration. 52. Sufentanil: Chloramphenicol increases sufentanil levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Sunitinib: Chloramphenicol increases sunitinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Suvorexant: Chloramphenicol increases suvorexant levels. This combination is contraindicated. 55. Tacrolimus: Chloramphenicol increases tacrolimus levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Tamsulosin: Chloramphenicol increases tamsulosin levels. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Tazemetostat: Chloramphenicol increases tazemetostat levels. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 58. Temsirolimus: Chloramphenicol increases temsirolimus levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Tezacaftor: Chloramphenicol increases tezacaftor levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 60. Tofacitinib: Chloramphenicol increases tofacitinib levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Tolterodine: Chloramphenicol increases tolterodine levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Tolvaptan: Chloramphenicol increases tolvaptan levels. This combination is contraindicated. 63. Toremifene: Chloramphenicol increases toremifene levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 64. Trabectedin: Chloramphenicol increases trabectedin levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 65. Trazodone: Chloramphenicol increases trazodone levels. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting drug regimens when chloramphenicol is used concurrently with other medications metabolized by CYP3A4.
